purpose: Phase F -- smallest practical single-worker calibration to distinguish concurrency amplification from intrinsic per-process growth, using 4 size-diverse not-started chunk0 pages.

worker.concurrent_with: chunk1 (PID 20471) remained running throughout -- calibration was NOT run in total isolation from all other load, but chunk0 was already dead so this was single-worker-plus-the-surviving-worker, not 2x-fresh-workers

pages_selected.method: size-diverse: smallest, median, 75th percentile, largest by image file size among chunk0's 196 not-started pages

result.exit_code_note: GENUINE exit code this time -- CALIBRATION_EXIT=0 confirmed, unlike chunk0's masked wrapper-vs-process discrepancy

pattern_observed: SPIKE-AND-RELEASE per page, not monotonic accumulation: RSS ramps up during each page's processing (likely during Docling layout/OCR inference, holding intermediate tensors/buffers) then drops back to a 2.7-2.9GB floor after each page completes and objects go out of scope. Peak scales loosely with image complexity (page 3 at 751KB peaked 5.34GB, page 4 at 1.9MB peaked 5.53GB -- only modestly higher for 2.5x the file size, so file size alone is not a strong linear predictor) but does NOT accumulate cumulatively across the 4 pages -- RSS returned to a similar ~2.7-2.9GB floor after every page, it did not ratchet upward page over page.

system_impact.chunk1_unaffected: chunk1 RSS stayed in its established 8.4-9.7GB band throughout, no coupling/amplification effect observed from the calibration worker running alongside it

chunk1_status_after_calibration: alive, healthy, RSS 8.99GB -- no incident during the ~5 minute calibration window despite a second process running concurrently
limitation: Only 4 pages tested (small n by design, per Phase F's own 'not statistical benchmarking' instruction). chunk0 itself looked healthy for 32 CONSECUTIVE pages in one continuous process before its fatal spike on page 33 -- this calibration does not fully replicate that exposure length. chunk1 has since safely exceeded that count (36 pages, continuous, no restart) which is directly relevant supporting evidence, but a dedicated long-run single-worker test has not been performed.
